newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND LOSE TWO KEY WICKETS BEFORE TEA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND LOSE TWO KEY WICKETS BEFORE TEA.

text.p: England lost two crucial wickets shortly before tea on Sunday as they began chasing the massive 469 needed to beat Australia in the third test.
Alec Stewart, who made just one, followed captain Michael Atherton back to the pavilion in successive overs.
At the interval England were 49 for two, and have to survive four more sessions just to force a draw.
Another capacity crowd, filling Old Trafford for the fourth successive day, sensed hope as openers Atherton and Mark Butcher raised 44 together without undue alarm.
Atherton even hooked Jason Gillespie for a fine six over square leg. But in the next over, the tall Australian had his revenge on the England captain, taking him leg before for 21.
The real test for England was always going to be how they coped with leg-spinner Shane Warne, whose six for 48 had destroyed their first innings.
In his third over, he fooled Stewart for the second time in the match, this time with a ball that kept straight to hit middle stump.
Mark Butcher was unbeaten on 25 at tea, but Australia were firm favourites to level the series at one each on the back of Warne's bowling and Steve Waugh's second century of the match.
Australia, 262 for six overnight, batted on until 20 minutes after lunch before declaring at 395 for eight and setting England a record fourth innings victory target.
